n1557216cff6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the E20 rollout?
o: Concerns include mileage reduction and possible damage to older vehicles.
E20 was to be sold with a minimum RON of 91 from 1 April 2026.
n1557216cff6.x: E20 was to be sold in all States and UTs with a minimum RON of 95 (not 91) from 1 April 2026. The other statements are correct.

n98833a3c6e4.s: Which of the following pairs (vehicular pollutant – health effect) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Carbon monoxide – Binds haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin
PM2.5 – Penetrates deep into lungs and bloodstream
Benzene – Forms ground-level ozone and acid rain
NOx – Respiratory illness, ground-level ozone and acid rain
n98833a3c6e4.x: Benzene is a carcinogen linked to leukaemia; it is NOx that forms ground-level ozone and acid rain.

nfea98330031.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CAFE III draft?
o: It proposes fuel-efficiency norms for cars from April 2027.
Its targets are about 21% stricter than the September 2025 proposal.
It provides credits for ethanol, CBG and biofuels.
It proposes a flatter weight curve.
nfea98330031.x: The CAFE III third draft (16 July 2026) has targets about 21% more relaxed, not stricter, than the September 2025 proposal.

n5ab76e2f1ac.s: BS-IV emission norms were implemented nationwide in India in:
n5ab76e2f1ac.x: BS-IV became applicable nationwide in April 2017; BS-III had gone nationwide in 2010.

n8b10b749a23.s: India's first vehicle emission norms for petrol vehicles came in:
n8b10b749a23.x: The first norms came in 1991 for petrol and 1992 for diesel vehicles; Euro-based Bharat Stage norms began in 2000.

ne1fd224555d.s: BS-VI norms became applicable to all new vehicles in India from:
ne1fd224555d.x: BS-VI became applicable to all new vehicles from 1 April 2020.

n53c77f1e8b4.s: BS-VI emission norms are equivalent to which European standard?
n53c77f1e8b4.x: BS-VI is equivalent to Euro 6; Euro 5 would have matched BS-V, the stage India skipped.

nca82034c615.s: The Chernobyl disaster is an example of:
nca82034c615.x: Chernobyl was a nuclear pollution accident; photochemical smog forms from NOx and hydrocarbons in sunlight.

ne026371c8e9.s: Euro emission norms cover carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and ____.
ne026371c8e9.x: The pollutants covered by Euro norms include carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and lead.

nenvironment-2-5.s: The National Auto Fuel Policy of 2003 was based on the report of which committee?
nenvironment-2-5.x: The Auto Fuel Policy (2003) followed the Mashelkar Committee report.

nenvironment-36-5.s: Bioremediation removes or detoxifies pollutants by using:
nenvironment-36-5.x: Bioremediation uses microorganisms to remove or break down pollutants; heavy metals like cadmium and lead limit it by poisoning the microbes.

n92157f6e033.s: What is the fuel-sulphur limit under BS-VI norms?
n92157f6e033.x: Sulphur limits fall from 500 ppm (BS-II) to 350 ppm (BS-III), 50 ppm (BS-IV) and 10 ppm (BS-VI).

na42b33148a5.s: In adopting equivalent emission standards, India has generally lagged Europe by about:
na42b33148a5.x: India generally lagged Europe by approximately five years in adopting equivalent emission standards.

n347e72db5ad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about industrial effluent management?
o: The Tiruppur textile cluster, cited as a Zero Liquid Discharge example, is in Andhra Pradesh.
Andhra Pradesh runs nine Common Effluent Treatment Plants.
Andhra Pradesh industries have been directed to adopt Zero Liquid Discharge.
Andhra Pradesh has banned discharge of non-biodegradable effluent.
n347e72db5ad.x: Tiruppur is in Tamil Nadu, not Andhra Pradesh. AP runs 9 CETPs, has directed ZLD and banned non-biodegradable effluent discharge.

n6790e48b9ee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about river pollution in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Godavari clean-up is linked to preparations for the 2027 Pushkarams.
The Namami Gange model is being applied to the Godavari basin.
Coal mines and cement plants are identified as the main water polluters.
Pharma City (Vizag), tanneries, paper mills and aquaculture are identified as main water polluters.
n6790e48b9ee.x: The main AP water polluters identified are Pharma City (Vizag), tanneries, paper mills and aquaculture, not coal mines and cement plants.

naa5048b168c.s:
Assertion (A): AMRUT 2.0 mandates 50 per cent reuse of treated urban wastewater.
Reason (R): The National Framework on Safe Reuse of Treated Water was issued in 2022.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
naa5048b168c.x: AMRUT 2.0 mandates 20 per cent (not 50 per cent) reuse, so A is false; the National Framework was indeed issued in 2022.

n5f9d7870deb.s:
Assertion (A): A water body with a very high BOD is heavily polluted.
Reason (R): BOD is the oxygen needed to oxidise all organic matter, both biodegradable and non-biodegradable.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5f9d7870deb.x: High BOD means heavy organic pollution, so A is true. R describes COD; BOD is the oxygen bacteria need to decompose organic matter, so R is false.

naa88d0225a2.s: The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) was launched at:
naa88d0225a2.x: GRCA was launched at COP28 in Dubai in December 2023 and is led by the NMCG under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

ne4455f7b2e6.s: The first dolphin estimate under the Namami Gange Mission (March 2025) counted how many dolphins?
ne4455f7b2e6.x: The first dolphin estimate (March 2025) counted 6,327 dolphins.

nec70ae3cb20.s: In fluorosis, fluoride replaces the hydroxyl group in hydroxyapatite, forming:
nec70ae3cb20.x: Fluoride replaces the hydroxyl group in hydroxyapatite, forming fluorapatite.

ndf483b98c26.s: Which sewage-treatment technology treats sewage in batches in a single tank?
ndf483b98c26.x: A sequencing batch reactor (SBR) treats sewage in batches in one tank; an MBR combines biological treatment with membrane filtration.

ncf69afcd7ea.s: Phase I of the Namami Gange Mission (2015-2020) had an outlay of:
ncf69afcd7ea.x: Phase I had ₹20,000 crore for 2015-2020; Namami Gange-II has ₹22,500 crore for 2021-2026.

nae02b453b43.s: In which year was the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) set up as the implementing arm of NGRBA?
nae02b453b43.x: NMCG was set up in 2011; NGRBA was constituted in 2009 and replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016.

nfa14610ea86.s: Under BIS IS 10500, the permissible limit of fluoride in drinking water is:
nfa14610ea86.x: BIS IS 10500 sets fluoride at 1.0 mg/L acceptable and 1.5 mg/L permissible.

n5bb7fd7cfc9.x: Methyl mercury biomagnified through fish and caused neurological damage in Minamata disease; cadmium causes Itai-itai disease.

n5515dcd3018.s: In 2016, the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) was replaced by:
n5515dcd3018.x: NGRBA, chaired by the Prime Minister, was replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016; NMCG (2011) was its implementing arm.

n5726536120b.s: In 2013 the National Lake Conservation Plan was merged with the wetlands programme to form:
n5726536120b.x: The National Lake Conservation Plan (2001) was merged with the wetlands programme to form NPCA in 2013.

n13d42b4178c.s: Under CPCB water-quality criteria, the minimum dissolved oxygen for Class B water is:
n13d42b4178c.x: Class A, B and C require at least 6, 5 and 4 mg/L of dissolved oxygen; Class D also requires at least 4 mg/L.

nbf428b0a0ef.s:
Assertion (A): Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment.
Reason (R): Article 48A provides for protection and improvement of the environment as a Directive Principle.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbf428b0a0ef.x: Both are true, but they are separate provisions: 51A(g) is a citizen's fundamental duty while 48A is a Directive Principle for the State, so R does not explain A.

ndedf093c9cd.s: Mercury pollution is mainly associated with:
ndedf093c9cd.x: Mercury is associated with chlor-alkali effluent and fungicides; chromates with tanneries, cadmium with phosphate fertilisers and batteries.

ndisaster-management-7-4.s: Which body is India's independent regulator for nuclear and radiation safety?
ndisaster-management-7-4.x: AERB is the independent safety regulator; DAE is the nodal technical agency with the Crisis Management Group.

naa8a8ad201f.s: Under the Contaminated Sites Rules, sites are tested against how many hazardous chemicals?
naa8a8ad201f.x: The Rules, made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, test sites against 189 hazardous chemicals.

n3be72f068bb.s: X-rays and isotopes belong to which category of radioactive pollution sources?
n3be72f068bb.x: Medical sources include X-rays and isotopes; natural sources include cosmic rays and radon-222.

nd36a9258e4e.s: After smoking, radon (Rn-222) is a leading cause of:
nd36a9258e4e.x: Radon, a radioactive noble gas that builds up indoors, is a leading cause of lung cancer after smoking.

n066af818b57.s: The night-time ambient noise limit for a residential area in India is:
n066af818b57.x: The residential night limit is 45 dB(A); the silence-zone night limit is 40 dB(A) and the industrial night limit 70 dB(A).

nd7bfd54662e.s: Which body approves the handling and disposal of radioactive waste in India?
nd7bfd54662e.x: AERB (1983, under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962) approves radioactive waste handling and disposal; the Environmental Survey Laboratory only monitors radiation.

n1fad7c4e5a2.s: CPCB bans firecrackers producing noise above ____ at 4 m from the point of bursting.
n1fad7c4e5a2.x: The CPCB limit is 125 dB at 4 m from the point of bursting.

n2341bb303e7.s: DDT, a persistent organic pollutant, is listed under which convention?
n2341bb303e7.x: DDT is a persistent organic pollutant listed under the Stockholm Convention.

n3e266d8f574.s: Adding nutrients to boost native microbes at a contaminated site is called:
n3e266d8f574.x: Biostimulation adds nutrients to boost native microbes; bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbes.

n5a0048037be.s: Oil Zapper, used against oil spills, is a:
n5a0048037be.x: Oil Zapper is a bioremediation agent, a TERI bacterial consortium, not a chemical dispersant.

n82c819d8da0.s: The GloLitter Partnerships (2019) is run by:
n82c819d8da0.x: GloLitter is run by the IMO and FAO, funded by Norway, and targets sea-based marine plastic litter.

n6a93272405f.s: India's first Dark Sky Reserve (2022) is located at:
n6a93272405f.x: Hanle in Ladakh, within Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, became India's first Dark Sky Reserve in 2022; Pench became the first Dark Sky Park in 2024.

n6c6154698b1.s: The build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil is called:
n6c6154698b1.x: Soil pollution is the build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil; it causes toxic crops and reduces vegetation.

n92ef600a1af.s: A rise of about how many decibels roughly doubles the perceived loudness of a sound?
n92ef600a1af.x: Every rise of about 10 dB roughly doubles perceived loudness.

n1dc3d39369b.s: Which of the following produces non-ionising radiation?
n1dc3d39369b.x: Cell towers produce non-ionising radiation, whereas X-ray machines produce ionising radiation.

nfe608bbf202.s: The IMO Ballast Water Management Convention came into force in:
nfe608bbf202.x: The Convention, which addresses the spread of invasive species through ballast water, entered into force in 2017.

n0fdc80e8aea.s: UCIL's Tummalapalle uranium mine and mill is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n0fdc80e8aea.x: Tummalapalle is in YSR Kadapa district, not Kurnool.

n6625532c845.s: How many Annexes does the IMO's MARPOL 73/78 convention have?
n6625532c845.x: MARPOL 73/78 is an IMO convention with six Annexes; it bans dumping of plastics at sea.

n26f9f6b9a81.s: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Anatomical waste and expired medicines – Yellow
n26f9f6b9a81.x: Contaminated recyclable plastics such as IV sets and catheters go into the Red category, not Yellow.

n7da3038717d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EPR under the E-waste Rules, 2022?
o: Producers receive annual recycling targets based on earlier sales.
Producers may buy digital EPR certificates from unregistered recyclers.
Producers register on the CPCB portal.
An EPR floor price is intended to protect formal recyclers.
n7da3038717d.x: Producers buy digital EPR certificates from registered recyclers, not unregistered ones.

nc6cfd145881.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: Plastics are classed as rigid, flexible and multi-layered.
Waste-to-energy, co-processing and waste-to-oil are permitted end-of-life options.
Unmet targets may be carried forward for up to five years.
nc6cfd145881.x: The 2026 amendment allows unmet targets to be carried forward for up to three years, not five.

ncbd53d2caee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about waste-to-energy technologies?
o: Incineration burns waste in the absence of oxygen.
Incineration can reduce waste volume by about 90 per cent.
Incineration may generate ash and emissions.
Biomethanation converts wet organic waste into biogas through microbial action.
ncbd53d2caee.x: Incineration burns waste in oxygen (and may produce steam for power); it does not work in the absence of oxygen.

n4828d3c71e7.s: Which of the following pairs (e-waste constituent – main harm) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Cadmium – Persistent nature and endocrine effects
Mercury – Brain and kidney damage; bioaccumulation in fish
Brominated flame retardants – Persistent nature and endocrine effects
n4828d3c71e7.x: Cadmium causes kidney and bone damage; persistence and endocrine effects describe brominated flame retardants (PBBs).

n3500854b351.s: Which of the following pairs (waste – preferred method) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Biomedical waste – Incineration at a common treatment facility
n3500854b351.x: High-calorific dry waste is used as RDF or co-processed in cement kilns, not landfilled.

nenvironment-40-7.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: UV purification – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen
Bioremediation – Using naturally occurring organisms to remove pollutants
Pyrolysis – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen to recover energy
nenvironment-40-7.x: UV purification kills microorganisms in drinking water; thermal breakdown without oxygen is pyrolysis.

ne2a51645a03.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanitary landfills?
o: Waste is compacted in cells and covered with earth daily.
They are intended for all biodegradable waste without segregation.
Liners and leachate-collection systems are used.
The method relies mainly on containment rather than treatment.
ne2a51645a03.x: Sanitary landfills are not meant for all biodegradable waste without segregation; the other features are correct.

n3a33ace913e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and their implementation?
o: Hill and island towns can levy user fees on tourists.
Hill and island bodies may regulate tourist inflow.
Environmental Compensation under the Rules is based on the precautionary principle.
The Supreme Court treated a clean environment as part of Article 21.
n3a33ace913e.x: Environmental Compensation follows the polluter-pays principle, not the precautionary principle.

n8d52a1c8d5e.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which bin–example pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Special care – Batteries, chemicals and paint cans
n8d52a1c8d5e.x: Wet waste covers food scraps, peels and garden waste; paper, plastics and metals go in the dry bin.

nd67b237c5b7.s: Which of the following pairs (convention – subject) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Basel – Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
nd67b237c5b7.x: The Rotterdam Convention covers Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides in trade; mercury is covered by Minamata.

n3bf7b0bd85c.s: Which of the following pairs (industrial waste – source) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Fly ash – Coal-based thermal power plants
n3bf7b0bd85c.x: Red mud comes from alumina refining; phosphogypsum comes from phosphoric acid or phosphatic fertiliser plants.

n34a97bb3bf6.s:
Assertion (A): Urban areas account for only about 20% of all waste generated in India.
Reason (R): As per official SBM-U figures, urban waste processing rose from 16% in 2014 to 82% in 2026.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n34a97bb3bf6.x: About 60% of waste comes from urban areas, so A is false; the SBM-U processing figures (16% to 82%) are correct.

nenvironment-40-8.s:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen is regarded as a clean fuel.
Reason (R): Hydrogen powers fuel cells that emit only water vapour.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nenvironment-40-8.x: Hydrogen fuel cells emit only water vapour, which is why hydrogen is considered a clean fuel.

n5f273a89414.s:
Assertion (A): Microbeads in cosmetics are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules.
Reason (R): An FSSAI study detected microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5f273a89414.x: Both statements are true, but the FSSAI food-sample finding does not explain the cosmetics microbead ban.

n12b9b57aae3.s:
Assertion (A): The INC-5.2 plastics treaty meeting in Geneva in August 2025 ended with no agreement.
Reason (R): Production caps, chemicals of concern and finance were major sticking points.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n12b9b57aae3.x: INC-5.2 ended without agreement because of disputes over production caps, chemicals of concern and finance.

n1d8d9276973.s:
Assertion (A): The E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022 came into force on 1 April 2023.
Reason (R): The 2022 Rules exclude solar PV modules, panels and cells.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n1d8d9276973.x: The Rules were notified in November 2022 and came into force on 1 April 2023, but their 106 EEE items include solar PV waste, so R is false.

nenvironment-26-4.s:
Assertion (A): Vermicomposting is a biological method of making compost.
Reason (R): Vermicompost is compost produced using earthworms.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nenvironment-26-4.x: Vermicompost is produced by earthworms, which is what makes it a biological composting method.

nae0cacf84e2.s: Under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016, which is at the top of the waste-management hierarchy?
nae0cacf84e2.x: Prevention is at the top of the hierarchy; co-processing comes later, before safe disposal.

n4df3111c6a7.s: Biomedical waste is waste arising from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of:
n4df3111c6a7.x: Biomedical waste arises from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals and includes blood, sharps, cultures and expired medicines.

nchemistry-8-43.s: Which of the following is an impact of non-biodegradable plastics?
nchemistry-8-43.x: Non-biodegradable plastics persist, pollute, break into microplastics, create landfill problems and harm wildlife.

nba3df798c1f.s: Swachh Survekshan, run by MoHUA under SBM-Urban, is conducted by:
nba3df798c1f.x: Swachh Survekshan, begun in 2016 under MoHUA, is conducted by the Quality Council of India.

ne7909d1426f.s: Which scheme aims to formalise informal sanitation and waste workers?
ne7909d1426f.x: The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers, who handle more than 70% of recycled plastic.

n99b19c6ba25.s: Solid waste includes discarded material in solid, liquid, semi-solid and ____ form.
n99b19c6ba25.x: The definition covers discarded or abandoned materials that are solid, liquid, semi-solid or containerised gaseous.

nenvironment-37-13.x: ITPGRFA covers plant genetic resources; Ramsar covers wetlands and Stockholm covers POPs.

n751929d97eb.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 was launched on:
n751929d97eb.x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021, runs till 2026, has an outlay of about ₹1.41 lakh crore and is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering all statutory towns.

n3f435069bb6.s: Under the Minamata Convention framework, dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by:
n3f435069bb6.x: The Minamata Convention concerns mercury, and dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by 2034.

nf7037ed1261.s: Anaerobic decomposition of biodegradable waste can produce:
nf7037ed1261.x: Anaerobic decomposition produces methane or biogas, while aerobic decomposition produces compost.

n1b6d91cb943.s: Phase I of SBM-Grameen aimed to construct over how many toilets by 2019-20?
n1b6d91cb943.x: Phase I aimed at over 10 crore toilets and ODF villages; rural sanitation coverage rose from 39% (2014) to 100% (2019).

n1ad562e5c35.s: As stated by the Chief Minister in February 2026, Andhra Pradesh inherited about how much legacy waste?
n1ad562e5c35.x: AP inherited about 108 lakh tonnes of legacy waste; Ongole is biomining its Guthikondavaripalem dump yard and supplying RDF to cement plants.

n1a7cd770bda.s: The Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025 took effect from:
n1a7cd770bda.x: The 2025 C&D Rules took effect from 1 April 2026; 1 October 2025 was the date in the draft SWM Rules.

nf6b643848fa.s: The highest of the three progressive levels of ODF Plus villages under SBM-Grameen is:
nf6b643848fa.x: ODF Plus levels run Aspiring, then Rising, then Model, which is the highest.

n23d5f63eb0a.s: Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) is mainly used as an alternative fuel in:
o: Cement kilns and thermal power plants
n23d5f63eb0a.x: RDF, made by shredding and dehydrating high-calorific MSW, is used in cement kilns and thermal power plants.

n11d04c0e19d.s: The Fly Ash Utilisation Notification requires use of fly ash in bricks, cement and roads within ____ of thermal plants.
n11d04c0e19d.x: The notification applies within 300 km of thermal plants; fly ash can make bricks and partly replace Portland cement.

nenvironment-39-4.s: Which of the following is a waste-to-energy process?
nenvironment-39-4.x: Pyrolysis (like plasma gasification) is a waste-to-energy process; compost and vermicompost turn waste into manure, not energy.

necf49ca50cf.s: Old municipal solid waste piled in dumpsites for years, emitting methane and polluting groundwater, is called:
necf49ca50cf.x: That is legacy waste; biomining excavates it and separates it into recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill.

n14bb81cab17.s: Surat is known for a road built using which industrial waste?
n14bb81cab17.x: Surat has a steel-slag road; steel slag is used as road base, to improve agricultural soil and in cement production.

n3d98d3aebed.s: Which was the first country to ban thin plastic bags, in 2002?
n3d98d3aebed.x: Bangladesh banned thin plastic bags in 2002; New Zealand's supermarket produce-bag ban came in July 2023.

nenvironment-37-10.s: Which of the following is biodegradable?
nenvironment-37-10.x: Sewage is biodegradable; plastic, DDT and asbestos are non-biodegradable.

n8ed6d3188ea.s: Which method of solid-waste disposal is described as not viable in urban India?
n8ed6d3188ea.x: Composting, incineration and landfilling are all used in urban India; only uncontrolled dumping is described as not viable.

nchemistry-8-10.s: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable polymer?
nchemistry-8-10.x: PVC is a non-biodegradable synthetic plastic; PHBV, starch and proteins are biodegradable polymers.

nda15a7722ba.s: Mercury-added products such as fluorescent lamps are being phased out under which convention?
nda15a7722ba.x: Mercury-added products are phased out under the Minamata Convention; Stockholm deals with persistent organic pollutants.

nb06a4b8655b.s: India's ban on identified single-use plastic items came into force on:
nb06a4b8655b.x: The SUP ban took effect on 1 July 2022; the EPR Guidelines on plastic packaging also became effective in July 2022.

nenvironment-37-4.s: Which Rio convention is associated with desertification?
nenvironment-37-4.x: The UNCCD covers desertification; the CBD covers biodiversity and the UNFCCC climate change.

n26751e623ea.s: APPCB has permitted how many cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste?
n26751e623ea.x: The APPCB permitted 12 cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste.

n17aad19669e.s: How many Municipal Corporations does Andhra Pradesh have, as stated in the context of urban waste management?
n17aad19669e.x: AP's urban set-up consists of 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.

nbb3a6f978c3.s: Which of the following was a provision of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016?
o: Unrestricted disposal of untreated waste in landfills
Extended producer responsibility for producers and brand owners
Exemption of brand owners from waste responsibility
nbb3a6f978c3.x: The 2016 Rules provided for user fees, spot fines and EPR for producers and brand owners, and prohibited untreated waste in landfills.

n41f395e3d6b.s: How many colour categories does the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 use?
n41f395e3d6b.x: The 2016 Rules use four colour categories with barcoding and GPS tracking; ten categories belonged to the 1998 Rules.

n8fe4dd43a60.s: From 31 December 2022, the minimum thickness of plastic carry bags in India is:
n8fe4dd43a60.x: Thickness rose from 40 (2011) to 50 (2016), 75 (30 September 2021) and 120 microns (31 December 2022).

n9aa2c8c5f80.s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, 'PIBOs' stands for:
n9aa2c8c5f80.x: EPR applies to Producers, Importers and Brand Owners (PIBOs) for plastic packaging not covered by the SUP ban.

n53f4a9d4ba6.s: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 replaced the battery rules of:
n53f4a9d4ba6.x: The 2022 Rules replaced the 2001 rules and cover EV, portable, automotive and industrial batteries under EPR.

n74018bad140.s: Which group of chemicals is often called 'forever chemicals'?
n74018bad140.x: PFAS persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging and can accumulate in animal bodies.

n766c896e325.s: In the municipal solid-waste collection chain, which step comes immediately before the Material Recovery Facility (MRF)?
n766c896e325.x: The chain runs door-to-door collection, segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing/recycling and residual landfill.

na0bce08e879.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)?
o: It was notified under Section 14AA of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
It is India's first mandatory compliance carbon market.
It is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.
na0bce08e879.x: Section 14AA belongs to the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, not the Environment (Protection) Act.

nenvironment-39-1.s:
Assertion (A): Blue carbon is carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems.
Reason (R): Geological storage of carbon uses coal seams, depleted oil and gas reservoirs and deep saline formations.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nenvironment-39-1.x: Both are true, but geological storage is a separate form of carbon storage and does not explain blue carbon.

n6ee827fffc8.s: The definitive phase of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) started on:
n6ee827fffc8.x: CBAM had a transitional phase from 2023 and its definitive phase began on 1 January 2026; certificates are priced on the EU ETS.

nde83b7412f0.s: REDD+ stands for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and ____.
nde83b7412f0.x: REDD+ is Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation; India takes part and forest conservation can earn tradable credits.

n5d7759178ec.s: Under which Article of the EU CBAM Regulation can a carbon price already paid, such as under India's CCTS, be deducted?
n5d7759178ec.x: Article 9 allows deduction of a carbon price already paid; CBAM revenue stays in Europe.

n77c2d76560b.s: The National Carbon Project is implemented under:
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change
n77c2d76560b.x: The National Carbon Project is under the ISRO Geosphere-Biosphere Programme and assesses carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biomes.

n59bfbb8de5f.s: The Gevra coal mine, listed among India's 'carbon bombs', is in:
n59bfbb8de5f.x: Gevra is in Chhattisgarh and Rajmahal in Jharkhand; a carbon bomb is a fossil project that could emit over 1 Gt CO2 in its lifetime.

nfdea976f1f3.s: Which footprint measures freshwater use as blue, green and grey water?
nfdea976f1f3.x: The water footprint counts freshwater use as blue, green and grey water; the ecological footprint is the land and water needed to support consumption and absorb waste.

n2cb420e446a.s: The carbon-removal method that pulls CO2 straight from ambient air is:
n2cb420e446a.x: Direct Air Capture pulls CO2 from ambient air; enhanced rock weathering spreads crushed silicate rock on land.

n6a4c9e9cf25.s: Which technology combines bioenergy with carbon capture and storage to give net-negative emissions?
n6a4c9e9cf25.x: BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) gives net-negative emissions.

n7f700b3ac8a.s: Which Union Territory's carbon-neutral effort includes solar water lifting, passive solar buildings, geothermal heating and electric vehicles?
n7f700b3ac8a.x: These measures are part of Ladakh's effort to become a carbon-neutral Union Territory.

na3a40d443b0.s: The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) under the Kyoto Protocol issues:
na3a40d443b0.x: The CDM issues Certified Emission Reductions (CERs); the VCS is run by Verra. One carbon credit equals one tonne CO2e.

ncd9f5984078.s: From FY 2025-26, coal-based power plants must co-fire what share of biomass?
ncd9f5984078.x: The co-firing requirement is 5% in FY 2024-25 and 7% from FY 2025-26, monitored by the SAMARTH mission.

n01d1f4b4a6f.s: India's 2035 NDC targets what cut in emission intensity compared with 2005?
n01d1f4b4a6f.x: The 2035 NDC targets a 47% cut in emission intensity vs 2005 and 60% non-fossil power capacity.

ncf531248edc.s: NET Power's Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant burns natural gas in oxygen and uses ____ as the working fluid.
ncf531248edc.x: The La Porte, Texas plant burns gas in oxygen with supercritical CO2 as the working fluid and captures nearly all its CO2.

nf2931b3d4d7.s: Emission-intensity targets for aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper were notified in October 2025 under:
nf2931b3d4d7.x: These sectoral emission-intensity targets were notified under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS).

n4e4e52c8f37.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Jan Vishwas reforms to pollution laws?
o: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act was passed in 2023.
It decriminalised minor offences under the Air Act and the Environment (Protection) Act.
The reforms replaced monetary penalties with imprisonment for minor offences.
The Water Act was amended likewise in 2024.
n4e4e52c8f37.x: The reforms replaced jail with monetary penalties for minor offences, not the reverse.

ne5be00795a0.s:
Assertion (A): The 1991 Ecomark scheme remains in force alongside the Ecomark Rules, 2024.
Reason (R): The Ecomark Rules notified in September 2024 aim to prevent misleading green claims and ensure accurate labelling.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne5be00795a0.x: The 2024 Rules replaced the 1991 scheme, so A is false; R correctly states their aim.

n7436a894375.s: Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) are meant to serve:
n7436a894375.x: CETPs serve clusters of small industries; SAAP (1992) gives grants to strengthen Pollution Control Boards.

nfaa0c0f6a4a.s: Under the 2026 Rules, the Environmental (Protection) Fund is shared between States/UTs and the Centre in the ratio:
nfaa0c0f6a4a.x: The Fund (Section 16, EP Act; audited by the CAG) is shared 75% States/UTs and 25% Centre.

n981494b741a.s: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) captures CO2 from:
o: Point sources such as cement plants
n981494b741a.x: CCS captures CO2 from point sources such as cement plants; it remains largely at the research stage.

n8e16c256865.s: APPCB allocates industrial inspections through a computerised system based on:
n8e16c256865.x: APPCB uses computerised, risk-based inspection allocation and has SOPs for effluents, marine outfalls and hazardous waste.

n2ce8bc56587.s: PM E-DRIVE (2024) is the successor to which scheme for electric mobility?
n2ce8bc56587.x: PM E-DRIVE (2024) gives EV and charging incentives, succeeding FAME; PM-KUSUM is for farm solar pumps.

n22e9f175ab2.s: Portland limestone cement is also known as:
n22e9f175ab2.x: Portland limestone cement is green cement, an example of green technology in the cement industry.

ne14a60015ee.s: Compared with conventional methods, bioremediation is:
ne14a60015ee.x: Bioremediation is eco-friendly and cost-effective but slower, and its results vary with local conditions.

n1678a92be40.s: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) cover how many pollutants?

nae991f5731f.s: In Andhra Pradesh's environmental initiatives, BRAP is associated with:
nae991f5731f.x: BRAP is associated with a single-window system, while APPCB is associated with siting guidelines.

ndisaster-management-1-12.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: NIDM – Premier institute for capacity building, training and research in disaster management
Aapda Mitra – Primary-level fund for immediate relief at the State level
State Disaster Response Fund – Immediate relief expenditure at the State level
National Disaster Response Fund – Response, relief and rehabilitation in severe calamities
ndisaster-management-1-12.x: Aapda Mitra is a scheme that trains community volunteers as first responders; it is not a fund.

ndisaster-management-28-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Sendai Framework targets (all by 2030)?
o: Target B – Substantially reduce disruption of basic services
Target A – Substantially reduce global disaster mortality
Target D – Substantially reduce disaster damage to critical infrastructure
Target D – Substantially reduce disruption of basic services
ndisaster-management-28-13.x: Target B is to substantially reduce the number of affected people globally; disruption of basic services falls under Target D.

ndisaster-management-25-8.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sendai Framework – Global blueprint for disaster risk reduction
National Disaster Management Plan – Operational plan implementing the National Policy and Sendai Framework
Prime Minister's 10-Point Agenda – Global blueprint for disaster risk reduction
National Policy on Disaster Management – Formulated in pursuance of the DM Act, 2005
ndisaster-management-25-8.x: The PM's 10-Point Agenda is India's action-oriented roadmap aligned with the Sendai Framework; the global blueprint is Sendai itself.

ndisaster-management-22-6.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: World Environment Day – Links environmental degradation with increased disaster risk
International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction – Core global DRR awareness day
World Meteorological Day – Observed on 22 April
ndisaster-management-22-6.x: 22 April is Earth Day; World Meteorological Day is the day declared by the World Meteorological Organization.

ndisaster-management-17-10.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Cabinet Committee on Security – Handles nuclear, biological and chemical emergencies
National Crisis Management Committee – Coordinates and directs responses to national crises
State Government – Responsible for post-disaster relief and rehabilitation
State Crisis Management Committee – Chaired by the Chief Minister
ndisaster-management-17-10.x: The State Crisis Management Committee handles state-level crises and is chaired by the Chief Secretary, not the Chief Minister.

ndisaster-management-28-4.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Sendai Framework priorities?
o: Priority 1 – Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience
Priority 4 – Enhancing preparedness for effective response and to 'Build Back Better'
Priority 3 – Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience
ndisaster-management-28-4.x: Priority 1 is understanding disaster risk; investing in DRR for resilience is Priority 3.

ne1b25eb6120.s: Which of the following pairs (framework – period or launch) is INCORRECTLY matched?
ne1b25eb6120.x: CDRI was launched in 2019; 2015 is the start of the Sendai Framework period.

n4caa15cf252.s: Which of the following pairs (disaster type – examples) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Biological disasters – Cyber attacks and space weather
Geological disasters – Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
Man-made disasters – Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Emerging disasters – Cyber attacks and space weather
n4caa15cf252.x: Biological disasters are epidemics and pest attacks; cyber attacks and space weather are emerging disasters.

ndisaster-management-34-4.s: With reference to cold-wave management, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Nodal agency for forecasting – India Meteorological Department
Agricultural measure – Frost protection techniques for crops
Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost (2021) – Issued by IMD
ndisaster-management-34-4.x: The 2021 Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost were issued by the NDMA; IMD is the forecasting agency.

nbc80e5cc38b.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no datable series)
nbc80e5cc38b.s: After August 2026, how many notified disasters are eligible for SDRF/NDRF assistance?
nbc80e5cc38b.x: The number rose to 14 after heatwave and lightning were added on the Sixteenth Finance Commission's advice; no man-made calamity is notified.

ndisaster-management-27-4.s: The UN office for disaster risk reduction was rebranded as UNDRR in:
ndisaster-management-27-4.x: The rename to UNDRR came in 2019; 1989–1999 was the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.

ndisaster-management-15-19.s: The NDRF's 2023 deployment to Turkey was called:
ndisaster-management-15-19.x: Turkey (2023) was Operation Dost; Myanmar (2025, after the Mandalay earthquake) was Operation Brahma.

n94d5ff66eba.s: Which of the following is primarily an earthquake mitigation measure rather than a cyclone measure?
n94d5ff66eba.x: Seismic zoning is primarily an earthquake mitigation measure; the others mitigate cyclones and storm surges.

n0cebdbc1a2e.s: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) is chaired by the:
n0cebdbc1a2e.x: NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister; it lays down policies and approves the National Plan.

ndisaster-management-27-9.s: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction was adopted on:
ndisaster-management-27-9.x: It was adopted on 18 March 2015 at the Third UN World Conference on DRR in Sendai, Japan.

n991a4559cee.x: Maitri assisted Nepal; Dost assisted Turkey and Syria, Karuna Myanmar, and Sadbhav Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar.

n85ef4d74a7e.s: In disaster management, susceptibility to harm is termed:
n85ef4d74a7e.x: Vulnerability is susceptibility to harm, with physical, social, economic and environmental dimensions.

ndf682c4e34e.s: The Bhopal Gas Tragedy at the Union Carbide India Ltd plant occurred on the night of:
ndf682c4e34e.x: The leak occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984; it was a man-made chemical hazard.

n5e00e5e794d.s: How many global targets does the Sendai Framework (2015–2030) contain?
n5e00e5e794d.x: The Sendai Framework has four priorities for action and seven global targets.

ndisaster-management-28-5.s: Sendai Framework Target G seeks to substantially increase:
o: Countries with national and local DRR strategies
Reduction of direct economic loss relative to GDP
Availability of and access to multi-hazard early warning systems
ndisaster-management-28-5.x: Target G widens access to multi-hazard early warning and risk information by 2030; Target C is economic loss and Target E is DRR strategies.

n0869718d13b.s: Chemical accidents in India are regulated under the MSIHC Rules, 1989 and the CAEPPR Rules of:
n0869718d13b.x: The MSIHC Rules 1989 and CAEPPR Rules 1996 govern chemical accidents; Crisis Groups exist at Central, State, District and Local levels.

ndisaster-management-32-5.s: Elderly people are listed under which type of vulnerable group?
ndisaster-management-32-5.x: The elderly are an age-based vulnerable group; coastal, Zone V, flood-plain and hill dwellers are location-based.

ndb973f16192.s: The ability of a community to resist, absorb and recover quickly from a hazard is called:
ndb973f16192.x: Resilience is the ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly; susceptibility to damage is vulnerability.

ndisaster-management-17-15.s: The NDMA and the NDRF both come under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
ndisaster-management-17-15.x: Both NDMA and NDRF come under the MHA, whose DM Division also strengthens Civil Defence and Home Guards.

ndisaster-management-12-15.s: Indian Standard IS 1893 is associated with:
ndisaster-management-12-15.x: IS 1893 governs earthquake-resistant design, a structural earthquake-mitigation measure.

ndisaster-management-25-9.s: India's first National Disaster Management Plan was issued in:
ndisaster-management-25-9.x: The first NDMP came in 2016; 2019 was its revision.

ndisaster-management-17-6.s: Who has overall disaster management responsibility at the district level?
ndisaster-management-17-6.x: The District Collector or District Magistrate is in overall charge of disaster management in the district; the community is usually the first responder.

ndisaster-management-17-5.s: Which ministry administers the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and runs the National Emergency Operations Centre?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
ndisaster-management-17-5.x: The MHA administers the DM Act, runs the National Emergency Operations Centre and coordinates international assistance and HADR.

ndisaster-management-12-11.s: Which of the following is a structural disaster-mitigation measure?
ndisaster-management-12-11.x: Retrofitting is structural mitigation, like earthquake-resistant buildings and sea walls; awareness and building codes are non-structural.

ndisaster-management-22-5.s: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) was raised in:
ndisaster-management-22-5.x: NDRF was raised in 2006, the year NDMA was also notified.

ndisaster-management-28-10.s: 'Strengthening disaster risk governance', which stresses laws, institutions, policies and coordination at all levels, is which Sendai priority?
ndisaster-management-28-10.x: Strengthening disaster risk governance is Sendai Priority 2; it emphasises laws, institutions, policies and coordination at every level.

ndisaster-management-28-16.s: Using recovery as an opportunity to reduce future disaster risk is called:
ndisaster-management-28-16.x: 'Build Back Better' uses recovery to reduce future risk.

ndisaster-management-34-11.s: Which body issued the cold-wave guidelines that focus on preparedness, vulnerability mapping and community awareness?
ndisaster-management-34-11.x: These are the NDMA's guidelines on cold waves.

ndisaster-management-20-14.s: Floods worsened by deforestation and landslides caused by unscientific construction are examples of:
ndisaster-management-20-14.x: They are socio-natural hazards, mixing natural processes and human action.

ndisaster-management-20-7.s: Industrial, chemical and nuclear disasters are classed as:
ndisaster-management-20-7.x: They are man-made (human-induced) because they arise from human activity, technology or negligence, not natural processes.

n2cd4fb51693.s: Under the Disaster Management Act, Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies have:
o: A legal role in local plans, relief and capacity building
No legal role in disaster management
Only an advisory role to the NDRF
n2cd4fb51693.x: The DM Act gives PRIs and ULBs a legal role in local plans, relief and capacity building.

nbf52ba6157b.s: How many Odisha villages have been recognised under the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready programme?
nbf52ba6157b.x: Twenty-four Odisha villages have been recognised; the target is 100.

ne19628af8b3.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) is chaired by the:
ne19628af8b3.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister and is the State's chief nodal agency for disaster management.

n88a05a73229.s: Andhra Pradesh now has India's ____ coastline and the longest on the east coast.
n88a05a73229.x: AP now has the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast; 'second-longest' is the older figure.

na27819c18c1.s: In disaster risk reduction, social media is best described as:
o: A complementary tool, not a replacement for official systems
A complete replacement for official warning systems
Useful only after the recovery phase
Of no use in community-based disaster management
na27819c18c1.x: Social media supports communication and community engagement but complements rather than replaces official systems.

ndisaster-management-33-11.s: 'Cool roofs' as a heatwave-management measure involve:
o: Reflective coatings or white painting of roofs
ndisaster-management-33-11.x: Cool roofs use reflective coatings or white paint to keep buildings cooler.

nc8d3fb07d5a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's legal framework for epidemics?
o: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for biological disasters.
The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was used during COVID-19.
The 2017 draft Public Health Bill was enacted and replaced the 1897 Act.
The 2017 draft Bill dealt with epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters.
nc8d3fb07d5a.x: The 2017 draft Bill was meant to replace the 1897 Act but was never enacted.

n840ef8869b3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disease surveillance in India?
o: IDSP was launched in 2004 and now runs under the National Health Mission.
The Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) was launched nationwide in 2018.
IDSP has a Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi.
IDSP works through State and District Surveillance Units.
n840ef8869b3.x: IHIP began in a few states in 2018 and went nationwide only from September 2021.

nc0859225d3c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about INSACOG?
o: Its full form is Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium.
It is a network of genome-sequencing laboratories that tracks SARS-CoV-2 variants.
It functions under DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW.
It was set up in December 2021.
nc0859225d3c.x: INSACOG was set up in December 2020, not 2021.

n821686164af.s:
Assertion (A): The National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) runs the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme and sends Outbreak Investigation Teams.
Reason (R): The National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre is run by DGHS, not NCDC.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n821686164af.x: A is true. R is false: NCDC (formerly NICD) itself runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre; DGHS is MoHFW's technical arm.

ne916b26ad90.s: The 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 made violence against health workers:
ne916b26ad90.x: The 2020 amendment (ordinance April, Act September 2020) made such violence cognizable and non-bailable.

n474a539d305.s: The 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations (2005) added a higher tier called:
o: Public Health Emergency of International Concern
n474a539d305.x: The 2024 amendments added a higher 'pandemic emergency' tier above the PHEIC.

n7f2159aeb70.s: NDMA's Biological Disaster Management guidelines were issued in:
n7f2159aeb70.x: NDMA, chaired by the Prime Minister, issued its Biological Disaster Management guidelines in 2008 under the DM Act.

n4ca7af0c04d.s: Isolation, quarantine and contact tracing belong to which phase of epidemic management?
n4ca7af0c04d.x: They are response measures; sanitation is mitigation, mock drills are preparedness and rehabilitation is recovery.

n57e5fff0f18.s: India's NDMP (2016) aligns with the Sendai Framework, the SDGs and the:
n57e5fff0f18.x: The 2016 NDMP aligns with Sendai (2015-30), the SDGs and the Paris Agreement and covers all phases of disaster management.

n0585e9e7647.s: Under PM-ABHIM, how many Integrated Public Health Laboratories are planned, one in every district?
n0585e9e7647.x: 744 IPHLs are planned, one per district; 631 is the number of Critical Care Hospital Blocks.

n65d23d6f92e.s: India's national COVID-19 lockdown of March 2020 was ordered under the:
n65d23d6f92e.x: The lockdown was ordered by NDMA and MHA under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

n34a8c1f0c40.s: Under the IHR (2005), Member States must report a possible PHEIC to WHO within:
n34a8c1f0c40.x: Member States must report possible PHEICs within 24 hours, build surveillance capacities and name a National IHR Focal Point.

nf4e3870535f.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on:
nf4e3870535f.x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025; the legally binding IHR (2005) have been in force since 2007.

n3103351a9b0.s: Mapping hotspots and containment zones during an epidemic chiefly uses:
n3103351a9b0.x: Geospatial technology supports contact tracing, hotspot and containment-zone mapping and vaccine distribution planning.

n205098876bc.s: Which of the following pairs (phytoremediation sub-type – process) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Phytoextraction – Contaminants stored in roots and shoots and the plant harvested
Phytodegradation – Plant enzymes break down organic pollutants
Phytovolatilisation – Contaminants released into the air in volatile form
Phytostabilisation – Contaminants released into the air in volatile form
n205098876bc.x: Phytostabilisation means roots immobilise contaminants and reduce leaching and erosion; volatile release is phytovolatilisation.

ne6d140a5a0b.s: Which of the following pairs (technique – application) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rhizofiltration – Injection of air under pressure below the water table
Mycoremediation – Use of fungi for treating organic pollutants
Rhizoremediation – Stimulation of rhizosphere microbes by plant roots
Biosparging – Injection of air under pressure below the water table
ne6d140a5a0b.x: Rhizofiltration is absorption or precipitation of contaminants from water by plant roots; air injection is biosparging.

nef444c648a7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bioremediation and conventional remediation?
o: Bioremediation is generally slower than conventional remediation.
Bioremediation can be scalable and community-applied.
Bioremediation has uniform reliability irrespective of pollutant, organism and site.
Conventional remediation is generally less dependent on site biology.
nef444c648a7.x: The reliability of bioremediation varies with the pollutant, organism, site and co-contaminants.

n2a432d73610.s: Which of the following pairs (institution – bioremediation role) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: CSIR-NEERI – Nodal bioremediation R&D, including heavy-metal removal
n2a432d73610.x: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S are TERI products; DBT-BIRAC funds biotech start-ups developing microbial kits.

ne613cbbdb8b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Visakhapatnam sewage-discharge issue?
o: The proposal favoured only large-scale pumping schemes.
It involved a PIL before the Andhra Pradesh High Court.
The stormwater drain passes through MVP Colony and Lawson's Bay Colony.
The drain enters the sea at Pedda Jalaripeta.
ne613cbbdb8b.x: Immediate bioremediation and decentralised STPs were proposed as a lower-cost alternative to pumping schemes.

n4b1c3ddb8e0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bioaugmentation and biostimulation?
o: Bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes into a site.
Biostimulation boosts existing microbes by supplying nutrients and oxygen.
TERI's Oilzapper is an example of bioaugmentation.
Adding nitrogen and phosphorus to polluted lakes is an example of bioaugmentation.
n4b1c3ddb8e0.x: Adding N and P to polluted lakes boosts existing microbes, so it is biostimulation, not bioaugmentation.

ne7505e310af.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no datable series)
ne7505e310af.s: Under the SWM Rules, 2026, landfills are intended only for:
ne7505e310af.x: Landfills are only for non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste; the Rules also mandate annual landfill audits.

n288866858d1.s: TERI developed Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S in collaboration with:
n288866858d1.x: These bacterial consortia were developed by TERI with Indian Oil to degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites.

nbiology-1-21.x: Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting, which first solved a murder investigation in England.

nbiology-40-8.s: In DNA fingerprinting, tissues from the same person show:
o: The same degree and pattern of polymorphism
Different polymorphism patterns in each tissue
Patterns inherited only from the mother
nbiology-40-8.x: One person's tissues share the same polymorphism pattern, and polymorphisms are inherited from parent to child.

n65d8342c260.s: The fern Pteris vittata is a hyperaccumulator of:
n65d8342c260.x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Alyssum accumulates nickel and Thlaspi caerulescens zinc and cadmium.

nbiology-39-10.s: Which of the following is a technique rather than a biological sample used in DNA fingerprinting?
nbiology-39-10.x: Biochips (like genetic diagnostics) are techniques; blood, saliva, skin, bone, hair follicles and sperm are biological samples.

nbiology-40-12.s: The human genome contains approximately how many DNA bases?
nbiology-40-12.x: The human genome has about 3 billion bases, over 99% of them shared among humans.

nbiology-40-10.x: CRISPR is used for genome editing; DNA sequencing serves molecular and genomic analysis.

n3ed307b9b75.s: Which bioremediation approach is the most cost-efficient and relatively passive?
n3ed307b9b75.x: In-situ treatment is the most cost-efficient and passive but slow; ex-situ bioreactors are the fastest.

nbiology-40-6.s: The sum total of expressed mRNA molecules in a cell is called the:
nbiology-40-6.x: The transcriptome is all expressed mRNA; the genome is the complete genetic information.

n941c71712ae.x: PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic; engineered Pseudomonas targets oil spills and biofilters treat air streams.

nbiology-9-4.x: Conjugation came from Lederberg and Tatum; restriction enzymes from Arber, Nathans and Smith.

nbiology-14-21.s: Who pioneered DNA fingerprinting in India?
nbiology-14-21.x: Lalji Singh pioneered DNA fingerprinting in India; Alec Jeffreys invented it in 1984.

nbiology-1-13.s: The first eukaryote to have its complete genome sequenced (1996) was:
nbiology-1-13.x: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) was the first eukaryote fully sequenced, in 1996.

nbiology-67-16.s: Which microorganisms are used as biofertilisers in paddy fields?
nbiology-67-16.x: Cyanobacteria are paddy biofertilisers; diatoms give diatomaceous earth and fungi give bread, alcohol and citric acid.

n48ccd151880.s: In phytoremediation, Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) is associated with accumulating:
n48ccd151880.x: Indian mustard accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium; sunflower accumulates uranium and other radionuclides.

nbc8106744b5.s: The key enzyme used in PCR to amplify DNA is:
nbc8106744b5.x: PCR uses DNA polymerase (denaturation, annealing, extension); ligase only joins DNA.

n52bac924bbd.s: For legacy dumps, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 make mandatory:
n52bac924bbd.x: The 2026 Rules mandate biomining/bioremediation of legacy dumps, alongside 'Lakshya Zero Dumpsites'.

neb01dc83dc2.s: The Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC), the national repository for publicly funded life-science data, is located at:
neb01dc83dc2.x: IBDC is at RCB, Faridabad, not CCMB Hyderabad.

nbiology-1-17.s: Samrupa was the world's first cloned:
nbiology-1-17.x: Samrupa was the first cloned buffalo; Dolly (Scotland, 5 July 1996) was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell.

nbiology-66-16.s: Aspergillus niger is used in fermentation to produce:
nbiology-66-16.x: Aspergillus niger makes citric acid; yeast makes ethanol, Lactobacillus lactic acid and Acetobacter acetic acid.

na9b61b74dbf.s: The symbiotic nitrogen fixer living in legume root nodules is:
na9b61b74dbf.x: Rhizobium is the symbiotic fixer in legume nodules; Azotobacter is free-living.

n482d7623a60.s: The first successful polio vaccine was developed by:
n482d7623a60.x: Jonas Salk developed the first successful polio vaccine; Albert Sabin developed the oral polio vaccine.

nd09df1c5fc3.s: The first genetically engineered oil-eating 'superbug' was developed by:
nd09df1c5fc3.x: The superbug was Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty; Ian Wilmut cloned Dolly.

ne1725d68c81.s: The BioE3 Policy (approved August 2024) stands for Biotechnology for:
ne1725d68c81.x: BioE3 means Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment; it promotes high-performance biomanufacturing.

nbiology-2-1.s: Injaz was the world's first cloned:
nbiology-2-1.x: Injaz was the first cloned camel; Samrupa was the first cloned buffalo and Ganga India's first cloned cow.

nae7d672d0a4.s: The hybridoma technique for monoclonal antibodies dates to:

nbiology-2-6.s: Ganga, a cloned cow, belongs to which breed?

nbiology-66-18.s: Which of the following is made by bacteria rather than yeast?
nbiology-66-18.x: Curd is made by Lactobacillus bacteria; wine, beer and bread use yeast.

nbiology-1-12.s: Who first identified transposable elements ('jumping genes')?
nbiology-1-12.x: Barbara McClintock first identified transposable elements.

nbiology-11-4.s: GM Mustard DMH-11 is associated with:
o: Prof. Deepak Pental and the Delhi University team
nbiology-11-4.x: DMH-11 is from Deepak Pental's Delhi University team; Mahyco made Bt brinjal and Gurdev Khush super rice.

nbiology-68-12.s: Lactobacillus, used in making curd, is a:
nbiology-68-12.x: Lactobacillus is a bacterium, not a fungus.

nbiology-2-5.s: The first heart transplant was performed by:
nbiology-2-5.x: Christian Barnard performed the first heart transplant, in South Africa; William Harvey described blood circulation.

nbiology-11-6.s: Lukoskin, developed by DRDO and DIBER, is used to treat:
nbiology-11-6.x: Lukoskin treats leucoderma; Eczit is for eczema and Amtooth for toothache.

nbiology-2-8.x: Triticale was the first man-made cereal.

nbiology-11-7.s: R21/Matrix-M, developed by Oxford's Jenner Institute and the Serum Institute of India, is a vaccine against:
nbiology-11-7.x: R21/Matrix-M is a malaria vaccine using Novavax's Matrix-M adjuvant.

nbiology-40-4.s: The complete genetic information or genetic makeup of an organism is its:
nbiology-40-4.x: The genome is the full genetic information; a zygote's genome combines DNA from two gametes.

nbiology-44-6.s: In an mRNA vaccine, the mRNA instructs the body's cells to produce:
nbiology-44-6.x: The vaccine mRNA makes cells produce the target antigen, which the immune system then responds to.

nbiology-2-3.s: DNA was first isolated in 1869 by:
nbiology-2-3.x: Friedrich Miescher isolated DNA in 1869; Watson and Crick proposed the double helix in 1953.

nbiology-2-10.s: India's first biodiesel plant was at:
nbiology-2-10.x: India's first biodiesel plant was at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh.

nbiology-11-5.s: The Dapog rice nursery method is associated with:
nbiology-11-5.x: The Dapog nursery method comes from the Philippines.

nbiology-67-11.s: Mushrooms belong to which group of microorganisms?
nbiology-67-11.x: Fungi give mushrooms and fermented foods, while bacteria make cheese, butter and curd.

nbiology-2-12.s: The first antibody produced during an infection is:
nbiology-2-12.x: IgM is the primary antibody, the first made in a new infection.

n64c8cfba9a0.s: The rising concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT or mercury along a food chain is called:
n64c8cfba9a0.x: That is biomagnification; bioremediation is the biological degradation or removal of pollutants.

n431ae785591.s: Cervavac, developed by the Serum Institute of India, targets:
n431ae785591.x: Cervavac is the Serum Institute of India's vaccine against HPV and cervical cancer.

n2db1df6d6bc.s: Bioaugmentation of an oil spill involves adding:
n2db1df6d6bc.x: Oil spills and oily sludge can be treated by bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria.

nd9f7fdcd3ca.x: Noori was a Pashmina goat (2012); Garima was a buffalo (NDRI, 2009) and Dolly a sheep (1996).

nd08741ee5e8.s: Which tree, planted along sewage ponds, transpires surplus wastewater?
nd08741ee5e8.x: Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater; mangroves and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators.

n4016de7a080.x: Blue biotechnology covers marine applications; red is medical, green agricultural and white industrial.

n7263b9782c1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Integrated Pest Management (IPM)?
o: Resistant varieties form one component of IPM.
Chemical control is the first and routine line of defence.
Crop rotation and changes in irrigation are cultural methods.
Traps and mulches are mechanical or physical methods.
n7263b9782c1.x: In IPM, chemical control is used only when needed, not routinely as the first option.

n0b4b72f9cf8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)?
o: It was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.
A standard cluster consists of 20 farmers covering 20 acres.
n0b4b72f9cf8.x: A standard PKVY cluster consists of 50 farmers covering 50 acres.

n758a09d515b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about organic-farming certification in India?
o: PGS-India is mainly associated with exports.
NPOP is based mainly on third-party certification.
NPOP is mainly associated with exports.
n758a09d515b.x: PGS-India is intended for the domestic market; NPOP is the export-oriented system.

n90c2af588ee.s: What is the total outlay of the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)?
n90c2af588ee.x: The total NMNF outlay is ₹2,481 crore; ₹897 crore is the States' share.

n23ccb03f229.s: Unlike the stricter approach of organic farming, sustainable agriculture may:
n23ccb03f229.x: Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously and include IPM and precision farming.

n818010bde6d.s: Biopesticides are an important IPM component mainly because they are:
o: Able to eliminate all pests permanently
Biodegradable, low in toxicity and short-lived
n818010bde6d.x: Biopesticides are biodegradable, comparatively low in toxicity and short-lived; they are not meant to eliminate all pests.

nf05a52e2b3c.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by:
nf05a52e2b3c.x: Subhash Palekar developed ZBNF; Bill Mollison and David Holmgren coined 'permaculture'.

n7fe945a9768.s: Charcoal produced by pyrolysis of biomass, used for long-term carbon sequestration in soil, is called:
n7fe945a9768.x: Biochar is pyrolysis charcoal that gives long-term carbon sequestration and water/nutrient retention.

ned4c536b8c9.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF) was formerly known as:
ned4c536b8c9.x: APCNF was formerly ZBNF; it uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham and covers over seven lakh farmers.

n616bf5a9ae1.s: Indiscriminate use of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides may result in:
n616bf5a9ae1.x: It can cause secondary pest outbreaks, pesticide resistance and contamination of ecosystems, soil and water.

nchemistry-16-35.s: Continuous use of chemical fertilisers leads to:
o: An increase in soil organic matter
A decline in soil organic matter
nchemistry-16-35.x: Continuous chemical fertiliser use depletes soil organic matter, reduces microbes and lowers nutrient density in food.

nchemistry-16-32.s: Excess nitrogen fertilisers leach ____ into groundwater.
nchemistry-16-32.x: Excess nitrogen acidifies soil, leaches nitrate into groundwater and causes eutrophication.

nchemistry-19-37.s: Chloropicrin, a broad-spectrum fungicide, herbicide and insecticide, is also used as a:
nchemistry-19-37.x: Chloropicrin is a broad-spectrum pesticide and also a tear gas.

nchemistry-19-50.s: Bordeaux mixture, a fungicide, contains copper sulphate and:
nchemistry-19-50.x: Bordeaux mixture is CuSO4 with Ca(OH)2 (lime).

nchemistry-16-6.s: Which plants are mainly used as green manure?
nchemistry-16-6.x: Green manure is a crop ploughed in while green; legumes are preferred because they fix nitrogen.

n03d318c88ee.s: India's first fully organic State is:
n03d318c88ee.x: Sikkim is the first fully organic State; PKVY was the first comprehensive organic-farming scheme.

n219814b772a.s: Natural farming is reported to reduce cultivation costs by about:
n219814b772a.x: Natural farming can cut cultivation costs by 20–40%, though it is knowledge-intensive and yields may dip during transition.
